EVERYDAY CAKE

Gluten-free
plum sponge cake

A tender butter sponge topped with juicy plum wedges and a gentle tartness.

Calculated

Quantities scaled. This version has not been bake-tested.

30 min
YIELD

DIFFICULTY

Total time: 1 hour

FLOUR

Ingredients
To shopping list…
Ripe but firm plums
800 g
Small eggs
10 pcs
Sugar
200 g
10 tbsp

240 g
12 tbsp

100 g

As needed
Salt
1 pinch
Vanillin
As needed
Method
Cook step by step

One step at a time, with ingredients and timers close at hand.

01
Prepare the pan and plums

Preheat the oven to 200°C. Line the pan with parchment and lightly butter the paper. Stone the plums, cut into wedges and pat away excess juice. Arrange in one layer with a cut surface against the paper.

02
Whip the whites and yolks separately

Separate the eggs. Beat the yolks with 4 tbsp of the sugar until pale. In a clean, dry bowl, whip the whites, gradually adding the remaining sugar. Gently fold the yolks into the whites.

CHECKPOINTThe whites hold their shape; the combined mixture remains airy.

03
Fold in the dry ingredients

TIPFirst, thoroughly mix the flour, tapioca starch, salt and vanillin, adding xanthan gum if using.

Fold the dry mixture into the egg mixture in several additions, lifting the batter from the bottom with a spatula.

CHECKPOINTNo dry pockets remain; the batter is still airy.

04
Fold in the butter

TIPMelt the butter before whipping the eggs so it has time to cool.

Melt 100 g butter and let it cool until just warm. Mix 3–4 spoonfuls of batter into the butter until smooth. Return this mixture to the main bowl and gently fold together.

CHECKPOINTThe butter is fully incorporated, with no oily streaks.

05
Cover the plums with batter

Spoon the batter over the plums in several places, then gently level it without moving the fruit. Put the pan straight into the preheated oven.

200°C · 30 MIN

06
Bake the cake

TIPIf the top browns before the centre is baked, cover loosely with foil and continue until done.

Bake at 200°C for about 30 minutes. To check, insert a skewer into the sponge, avoiding the fruit.

CHECKPOINTThe top is golden, the centre springs back gently and the skewer has no raw batter.

07
Invert and cool

Remove the cake from the oven and loosen the edges. Wearing oven mitts, cover the pan with a larger flat platter and turn both over together. Lift off the pan and carefully peel away the parchment. Let the cake cool before slicing.

Gluten-free
apple fritters

Tender gluten-free apple fritters with Schär Mix B Bread.

Calculated

Quantities scaled. This version has not been bake-tested.

ACTIVE TIME

YIELD

DIFFICULTY
Easy

A handy rule of thumb: one large apple per person.

FLOUR
Schär Mix B Bread

Ingredients
To shopping list…
Apples
Peel and grate coarsely.
6 pcs
Eggs
4 pcs
Kefir or natural yoghurt
300 g
Schär Mix B Bread flour
200 g
10 tbsp
Sugar or a ripe soft banana
Use the sugar amount shown. To replace it, mash one ripe soft banana per tablespoon of sugar.
2 tbsp
Bicarbonate of soda
6 g
1 tsp
Oil for frying
As needed
Method
Cook step by step

One step at a time, with ingredients and timers close at hand.

01
Prepare the apples

Wash and peel the apples, then grate them on the coarse side of a grater. Do not grate them finely, or they will release too much juice.

CHECKPOINTThe apples are in distinct coarse shreds rather than a fine, wet pulp.

02
Mix the batter

Crack the eggs directly into the grated apples. Add the kefir or yoghurt and the sugar, or the mashed banana instead of sugar, then mix. Add the Schär Mix B Bread flour and bicarbonate of soda and stir until combined.

2–3 MIN PER SIDE · MEDIUM HEAT

03
Fry the fritters

TIPLower the heat if the outside browns before the top begins to set.

Heat a little oil in a frying pan. Spoon 1 tablespoon of batter per fritter into the hot pan and fry over medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side, so the apples have time to cook through.

CHECKPOINTTurn when the underside is golden and the top has begun to set around the edges; the centre should no longer look wet after the second side cooks.
